regions.text: 我々は經驗地平におけると形而上約地平におけるとによつて必然および偶然の意味が正反對になつてゐることに無づく。

quote.translation: We notice, then, that the meanings of the necessary and the contingent are directly reversed according to whether we stand on the empirical horizon or on the metaphysical horizon.

regions.text: 経驗内地平は「下より」の行き万で、因果前必然の系列を無限に避って、原始偶然へ到達する（一^三風参照）。

quote.translation: The empirical horizon proceeds "from below", going back infinitely along the series of causal necessity until it arrives at primal contingency (see p. 183).

regions.text: 形面上約地平は「上より」の行き方で、絶對前必然の否定として、因果性のうちに騰にせられた偶然の機念を得る。換言すれば因果性によつて規定せられることは、経駿的見地よりは必然と云はれ形而上見地よりは偶然と云はれる。

quote.translation: The metaphysical horizon proceeds "from above", and obtains, as the negation of absolute necessity, the concept of the contingent held captive within causality.

quote.translation: In other words, being determined by causality is called necessary from the empirical standpoint and contingent from the metaphysical standpoint.

regions.text: また、因果系列の起始が理念として把握せられるとき経驗的見地よりは原始偶然と云はれ、同じ理念が形而上約見地よりは離接必然の形に於て絕對的必然と云ばれる。すなばち必然性には「懸對的必然と假説必然との區別がある。

quote.translation: Again, when the beginning of the causal series is grasped as an idea, it is called primal contingency from the empirical standpoint, whilst the same idea is called absolute necessity, in the form of disjunctive necessity, from the metaphysical standpoint.

quote.translation: Within necessity, that is to say, there is a distinction between "absolute necessity" and "hypothetical necessity".

regions.text: ibniz,Operaphilosophica,ed.Erdmann,p793）クリスティアン・ウォルフによれば『必然存在とはその存在が知謝脚に必然（absolutenecessari）のものである。偶然存在とは、自己の存在の理由を自己の外に有するものである。従つて「偶然存在の存在は單に假説的に必然（bypotheticenecessariaz）である』（ChristianWoif,Ontologia.

quote.translation: Leibniz too drew the distinction between "absolute necessity" (nécessité absolue) and "hypothetical necessity" (nécessité hypothétique) (Leibniz, Opera philosophica, ed. Erdmann, p. 763), and according to Christian Wolff, "necessary existence is that whose existence is absolutely necessary (absolute necessaria); contingent existence is that which has the ground of its own existence outside itself", so that "the existence of contingent existence is merely hypothetically necessary (hypothetice necessaria)" (Christian Wolff, Ontologia, § 309f., § 316).
